review_notes: I read the whole file. I grepped the SchwarzChristoffel directory for existing bundles or named definitions of the total exponent and found none. The directory has no `structure` for the (a, e) data, and `schwarzChristoffelPolygon` in Polygon/Basic.lean is a different object. The repeated interval hypothesis `∀ i, e i ≠ 0 → a i ∉ Ioo p q` (63 occurrences in 14 files) is a candidate for a named predicate. I judged it only optional packaging, so I did not report it. The finding below is about the unnamed total-exponent function. It is a modest improvement: a plain `def` would be enough, and a `Finsupp` or bundled form is optional. I did not check how every one of the roughly 276 uses would look after a rewrite, and I did not check import ordering. A definition in Vertex.lean should avoid cycles, since Vertex.lean is already imported by this file.

findings.excerpt: (he : ∀ x ∈ s, -1 < ∑ i with a i = x, e i)
findings.problem: The 'total exponent at x', defined as the sum of the exponents of all prevertices located at x, is a central mathematical object here. The docstrings call it the 'total exponent' throughout, and it is the exact integrability criterion (> -1) and the vanishing criterion on prevertex-free intervals. It has no name or bundled form. Every statement spells out the raw expression `∑ i with a i = x, e i`. The sum_filter_eq_zero_of_mem_Ioo lemma exists only to recover facts about this function. The same raw expression occurs about 276 times across 46 files of the SchwarzChristoffel directory, for example in Corner/Basic.lean and UnboundedEdge.lean. Hypotheses such as `-1 < ∑ i with a i = x, e i` need a Finset.filter, and a DecidableEq instance on ℝ, in each statement. A rewrite also has to match that syntactic shape. The hypothesis `∀ x ∈ s, -1 < …` is really a statement about the function x ↦ total exponent.
findings.proposed_change: In Vertex.lean, or at the top of this file, define the total exponent once. A plain `def schwarzChristoffelExponentAt (a e : ι → ℝ) (x : ℝ) : ℝ := ∑ i with a i = x, e i` is enough. A bundled version could instead be the finitely supported function `Finsupp.mapDomain a (Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite.symm e) : ℝ →₀ ℝ`, which is the exponent 'divisor' on the real line. Add a simp lemma `schwarzChristoffelExponentAt_eq_sum`, and a lemma stating that the function vanishes at x when no prevertex of nonzero exponent lies in an interval around x, which is the content of `sum_filter_eq_zero_of_mem_Ioo`. The consumer then becomes `(he : ∀ x ∈ s, -1 < schwarzChristoffelExponentAt a e x)`. The Icc proof reduces to `hp`, `hq`, and the vanishing lemma applied at interior points.
findings.benefit: Statements become shorter and easier to read, and they match the 'total exponent' wording of the docs. Proofs that handle the exponent at a point (`he`, `hp`, `hq`) no longer depend on a particular Finset.filter spelling. The support of the Finsupp form would give the set of prevertices with nonzero exponent. That set is what the repeated hypothesis `∀ i, e i ≠ 0 → a i ∉ Ioo p q` expresses. Fixing the definition once would also make later changes to it, such as merging coincident prevertices, local to one place.
